newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Leonid Sodoley loading 20,555 tonnes soybeans. Derby North loading 47,000 tonnes soymeal. Tiger Island loading 25,700 tonnes soymeal. Ocean Friend loading 40,000 tonnes soymeal. Walka Mlodych loading 28,200 tonnes soymeal. Waiting to dock, three vessels for soybeans, two for mixed cargoes (soybeans/meal) and seven for soymeal.
Road: 2,018 trucks carrying soybeans arrived between May 23 and 25, 834 trucks with soymeal and 156 with vegetable oils, including soyoil.
Loading: Between May 23 and 25, 41,924 tonnes soybeans and 54,027 soymeal were loaded at the port.
Stocks: No figures available. NOTE: Rain slowed the loading of grains over the weekend, with the port terminal functioning on an on/off basis as the weather permitted.
Vessels: No vessel loading at port terminal, at Cargill private terminal Petimata Ot Rms loading 31,000 tonnes soymeal. No vessels waiting to dock.
Road: 132 trucks carrying 3,506 tonnes soybeans arrived on May 25.
Rail: Eight wagons arrived carrying 522 tonnes soybeans.

NOTE: Although it rained over the weekend, loading of soybeans and soy products at the public terminal was not affected as there were no vessels docked to load these products. However, loading of wheat, salt and fertilizers was slowed.
